nodes.label: CubeSat Design Specification (CDS)
nodes.author: Cal Poly
nodes.rationale: General requirements for all CubeSats, usable for preliminary design, but not the official launch requirement set (the mission ICD is).

nodes.label: CubeSat 101: Basic Concepts and Processes for First-Time CubeSat Developers
nodes.author: NASA CubeSat Launch Initiative / Cal Poly CubeSat Systems Engineer Lab
nodes.norm_label: cubesat 101: basic concepts and processes for first-time cubesat developers
nodes.rationale: Written because little information exists for someone just entering the CubeSat field; aimed at first-time and educational developers (Oct 2017 revision).

nodes.label: LSP-REQ-317.01 Program Level Requirements
nodes.author: NASA LSP
nodes.rationale: Ensures CubeSats and dispensers add no risk to the primary payload.

nodes.label: Flight Certification Documentation
nodes.rationale: Verification evidence that CubeSat meets every mission requirement; first deliverable ~10 months before delivery; keep integrator aware of all design changes.

nodes.label: Thermal Vacuum (TVAC) Bakeout Testing
nodes.rationale: Forces outgassing in the lab so contaminants are not released near the sensitive primary payload.

nodes.label: TVAC Cycling
nodes.rationale: Optional internal test screening thermal-cycle failures (solder joints, batteries); cannot replace bakeout.

nodes.label: Dynamic Environment Testing (Vibration/Shock)
nodes.rationale: Vibration required for all launches, shock not always; after testing no physical changes allowed.

nodes.label: Compliance Letter
nodes.rationale: Signed by the principal investigator; certifies e.g. no pressure vessels, propulsion or explosives, and no transmissions until 45 minutes after deployment.

nodes.label: Mission-Specific Interface Control Document (ICD)
nodes.rationale: The official rulebook: CubeSat-to-dispenser ICD (by integrator) plus dispenser-to-LV ICD; captures CDS, range safety and environmental test levels. Failing any requirement may mean not flying.

nodes.label: Missile System Prelaunch Safety Package (MSPSP)
nodes.rationale: Covers all hazards to LV, dispenser, other CubeSats and personnel; due at least 45 days before arrival at the range.

nodes.label: Testing Procedures/Reports
nodes.rationale: Report every anomaly; stop test and notify integrator. Get procedures reviewed first or risk retesting flight hardware.

nodes.label: Venting Analysis
nodes.rationale: Rapid ascent depressurization could burst trapped air pockets and endanger LV and other payloads.

nodes.label: Amateur License (FCC Part 97)
nodes.rationale: Hardest to qualify for: no government or commercial involvement, no encryption; FCC looks at operator, NOAA at owner.

nodes.label: Experimental License (FCC Part 5, Form 442 / STA)
nodes.rationale: Typical for university/CSLI CubeSats; STA for experiments under six months, Form 442 for longer.

nodes.label: Federal Communications Commission (FCC)
nodes.rationale: Requires minimum 90 days from application receipt to license issuance.

nodes.label: Federal Statutes (47 CFR Part 97, 15 CFR Part 960)
nodes.norm_label: federal statutes (47 cfr part 97, 15 cfr part 960)

nodes.label: International Amateur Radio Union (IARU)
nodes.rationale: Volunteer body that assigns amateur-band frequencies; slow review cycles mean requests should go in immediately after manifest.

nodes.label: Launch
nodes.rationale: Only the primary mission or LV can move the date; scrubs common, so budget extra travel days.

nodes.label: Regulatory Licensing
nodes.rationale: Lengthy; apply within 30 days of manifest. Missing licenses at delivery means demanifest; an early CubeSat nearly had its release mechanism disabled awaiting FCC approval.

nodes.label: NOAA Remote Sensing License (CRSRA)
nodes.rationale: Any non-federal CubeSat with an imager must apply; Earth-only imaging approval ~120 days; developer solely responsible; post-launch audits required.

nodes.label: Radio Frequency (RF) Licensing
nodes.rationale: License types: amateur, commercial (Part 25), experimental, government. Experimental CubeSats must operate non-interference and be able to cease emissions.

nodes.label: Mass Properties Report
nodes.rationale: Total mass, CG, MOIs; LV provider load analyses depend on it, so out-of-tolerance final numbers can mean demanifest. Include large but reasonable margins on early estimates.

nodes.label: Demanifest Risk
nodes.rationale: CubeSats are bumped for missing funds, missing licenses, out-of-tolerance mass properties, or late delivery; the LV leaves without them since CubeSats have no influence on the launch date.

nodes.label: Announcement of Partnership Opportunity (AoPO)
nodes.rationale: Posted early August, proposals due November; non-compliant proposals are removed from consideration.

nodes.label: NASA CubeSat Launch Initiative (CSLI)
nodes.rationale: NASA covers launch cost (up to ~$300,000, typically a 3U to LEO) in exchange for a report on investigation results; investigations must benefit NASA Strategic Plan goals.

nodes.label: Example CSLI CubeSat Missions (LightSail, KickSat, MinXSS, BisonSat, STMSat-1, TJ3Sat, Dellingr)
nodes.norm_label: example csli cubesat missions (lightsail, kicksat, minxss, bisonsat, stmsat-1, tj3sat, dellingr)

nodes.label: Selection and Manifesting
nodes.rationale: Selection Recommendation Committee prioritizes; LSP pairs CubeSats with launches by orbit and completion date. Priority gives 'dibs' on the first matching launch.

nodes.label: Securing Funding
nodes.rationale: Developers pay all build, test, ground station, ops and travel costs; running out of money after manifest loses the slot and may trigger CRADA reimbursement. Keep 10% reserves; sources include RFPs, NSF, ESTO, Space Grant, crowdfunding, technology demonstration sponsors.

nodes.label: Orbital Debris Assessment Report (ODAR)
nodes.rationale: Shows CubeSat poses no unacceptable hazard, deorbits in reasonable time, and no large piece survives reentry; generated by NASA LSP for CSLI CubeSats; prefer low-melting-point materials (aluminum over titanium/tungsten).

nodes.label: Keys to CSLI Selection
nodes.rationale: Adequate funding, great merit and feasibility reviews, clear benefit to NASA; keep launch requirements flexible.

nodes.label: CubeSat Dispenser
nodes.rationale: Interface between CubeSat and launch vehicle: attaches to LV, protects CubeSat, opens door on LV command to eject it. Developer usually does not choose it.

nodes.label: CubeSat-to-Dispenser Integration and Testing
nodes.rationale: Two days: day 1 measure and insert, day 2 final vibration of dispenser+CubeSat; after this the developer loses access.

nodes.label: ISS Deployment Mission Model (NanoRacks)
nodes.rationale: CubeSats ride in pressurized cargo (Dragon, Cygnus) and astronauts deploy them 1-3 months after arrival; NanoRacks was the only commercial ISS deployer.

nodes.label: Launch Vehicle (LV)
nodes.rationale: CubeSats ride as auxiliary payloads; LV must have margin, go to the desired orbit, and accept dispensers. Includes Super Strypi, Minotaur, Taurus XL, Delta II, Antares, Falcon 9, Atlas V, Electron, SLS.

nodes.label: Mission Models
nodes.rationale: Different sponsoring organizations run missions differently, but from the developer's view all involve tag-ups with an integrator, document submission, and a readiness review.

nodes.label: National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) Rideshare Mission Model
nodes.norm_label: national reconnaissance office (nro) rideshare mission model
nodes.rationale: Developers work with the Auxiliary Payload Integration Contractor (APIC) under the Office of Space Launch (OSL).

nodes.norm_label: operationally responsive space (ors) rideshare mission model

nodes.norm_label: commercial launch through third-party broker mission model

nodes.label: CubeSat
nodes.rationale: Begun 1999 by Jordi Puig-Suari (Cal Poly) and Bob Twiggs (Stanford SSDL) to give affordable access to space; standardization lets vendors mass-produce COTS parts and lowers transport/deploy costs.

nodes.label: CubeSat Unit (1U, 1.5U, 2U, 3U, 6U, 12U)
nodes.rationale: 1U = 10 cm cube, ~1-1.33 kg; 6U (2014) is two 3Us side-by-side.

nodes.label: UL Listed Batteries
nodes.rationale: Uncertified or modified batteries trigger extra robustness testing by the launch provider.

nodes.label: CubeSat Acceptance Checklist (CAC)
nodes.rationale: Per-size limits: 1U <1.33 kg/113.5 mm, 1.5U <2.00 kg, 2U <2.66 kg, 3U <4.00 kg/340.5 mm; 100 +/- 0.1 mm width; protrusions and RBF pin <= 6.5 mm.

nodes.label: CubeSat Design Advice (keep simple, don't design to envelope limits, double burn wire, familiar components, UL batteries)
nodes.norm_label: cubesat design advice (keep simple, don't design to envelope limits, double burn wire, familiar components, ul batteries)
nodes.rationale: Derived from real mishaps: propulsion/pyrotechnics make launch providers nervous; if it doesn't fit it doesn't fly; important components on exterior ease rework after test failures.

nodes.label: Day In The Life (DITL) Testing
nodes.rationale: Simulates ejection by pulling RBF pin and releasing separation switches, timing deployables and first transmission; after DITL no flight software may change.

nodes.label: Electrical Inhibit
nodes.rationale: Interrupts the power path; an independent inhibit is a physical device between power source and hazard, a timer does not count.

nodes.label: Engineering Test Unit (ETU)
nodes.rationale: Cheaper to build multiple units at once (ETU, FlatSat, two flight units) and fly the best hardware.

nodes.label: Mission Readiness Review (MRR)
nodes.rationale: In-person half-day presentation of evidence that ICD is met; all testing done and deliverables accepted beforehand; draft due 2 weeks prior.

nodes.label: Development Testing vs Verification Testing
nodes.rationale: Development testing is internal and unlimited ('test like you fly'); verification testing proves ICD compliance and after it the CubeSat cannot be touched without retesting.

nodes.label: Ground Station
nodes.rationale: Needs at least radio and antenna; launching with an inadequate ground station is a mission killer, so build early and practice tracking existing satellites (437 MHz CubeSats, 140 MHz NOAA weather sats).

nodes.label: Mission Integrator
nodes.rationale: Coordinates schedules, deliverables and requirement verification between LV provider and developers; issues the mission ICD; coordination starts ~18 months before launch with a kickoff telecon.

nodes.label: Mission Operations
nodes.rationale: First challenge is identifying which new object is yours; can take weeks. Amateur trackers and the CubeSat IRC channel help with first contacts.
